claim: The Register 2026-11-03: Raspberry Pi raised the 16GB Pi 5 by $80 to $385 (launched Jan 2025 at $120; +$25 Dec 2025, +$60 Feb 2026, +$100 Apr 2026) and the 16GB CM5 variants by $40; in early Oct 2026 the 2GB Pi 5 rose $12.50 to $77.50; Upton cites 'a lack of alternative supply for 16GB DRAM' and calls the landscape 'ultimately temporary'. 4GB/8GB Pi 5 prices are not stated in the article.

Hardware Busters 2026-07-21: NVIDIA's US price table raised Jetson prices with no announcement: Orin Nano Super devkit $249 to $399 (+60%), AGX Orin devkit $1,999 to $3,499 (+75%), AGX Thor devkit $3,499 to $5,499 (+57%), AGX Orin 32GB module $899 to $1,799 (+100%); NVIDIA gave no reason (memory cost is the author's inference)

Sidero Labs blog 2026-09-14: Sidero Labs has joined Yardi (acquired); 'Talos Linux remains fully open source under the MPL-2.0 license - same repos, same license'; continues as a standalone company 'with the same team'; the post makes no commitment on Omni licensing or product pricing

Sidero Labs pricing page (read 2026-11-11): Talos Community $0 (MPL-2.0); Talos Enterprise Linux $1,000 per node per year, 10-node minimum, Omni included; Omni Hobby free up to 10 nodes and 2 users; Omni Startup $25 per node per month up to 50 nodes; Omni Edge 'Priced for edge scale', no public price (contact sales)

kairos-io/kairos issue #2010 'Support for Raspberry Pi 5': open since 2023-11-17, no milestone; a member wrote 2025-11-26 that SUSE's rpi5 work is 'still incomplete' and 'Im not sure how much we can dedicate to this topic'; a bot triage comment 2026-09-03 says nothing in the tree supports rpi5 yet; a bot set roadmap status 'Q2 2027' on 2026-11-09

siderolabs/sbc-jetson PR #23 (Orin support): still open, no formal review submitted; project-board status 'On Hold' since 2026-02-18; last PR comments 2026-04-20/22 (a maintainer: wants to get it merged); latest linked activity is a community fork (schwankner/talos-jetson-orin) on 2026-09-11; a commenter notes NVIDIA's gpu-operator does not support Jetson

siderolabs/talos issue #12748 (opened 2026-02-08): Talos 1.12.3 kernel-panics at boot on a Raspberry Pi 5 Rev 1.1 with BCM2712 D0 stepping (also reported on CM5); maintainer: the D0 overlay comes from the Raspberry Pi kernel and is incompatible with Talos naming, and they had tested only C stepping; workaround is deleting an overlay file; issue closed with linked sbc-raspberrypi PR #79

siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi issue #23 'RPi5 is unable to boot' (2024-10-03, Talos 1.8.0): reporter notes Pi 5 NVMe and Ethernet need the Raspberry Pi kernel because RP1 is not fully supported in mainline; closed via PR #71; the visible thread does not state that the official overlay boots from NVMe
